facts.statement: The genus is known from a single holotype fossil collected by William Nava, which gives the species its specific name navae.
facts.quote: It is known from only one fossil, holotype UFRJ-DG 107-R, collected by William Nava (hence the specific name navae).

facts.statement: The fossil, consisting of a partial skull, limb bones, and vertebrae, was discovered 25 km southwest of Marilia near a reservoir dam.
facts.quote: The fossil consists of a partial skull, fragmentary limb bones and a few broken vertebrae, and was found 25 km southwest of the town of Marilia, near a reservoir dam.

facts.statement: The skull was small, measuring only 60 mm in length and 30 mm in height, with very large elliptical orbits nearly as long as the rostrum, suggesting the animal might have been nocturnal.
facts.quote: The skull is small, only 60 mm long and around 30 mm high, but the elliptical orbits are very large, almost as long as the rostrum, which might suggest the animal was nocturnal.

facts.statement: The maxilla bears seven molariform teeth of varying sizes, supporting the theory of its placement in the sphagesaurid group.
facts.quote: The maxillary dentition appears to bear out this theory as it bears seven molariform teeth of varying sizes.

facts.statement: The teeth of Adamantinasuchus are noticeably heterodont, featuring a mixture of incisiform, caniniform, and molariform types.
facts.quote: The teeth are noticeably heterodont in Adamantinasuchus, with a mixture of incisiform, caniniform and molariform teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Adamantinasuchus might have had an omnivorous diet including plants, similar to Chimaerasuchus, due to its heterodont teeth and well-developed molariform teeth.
facts.quote: Adamantinasuchuss teeth seem to be quite well adapted for an omnivorous diet, since they are heterodont and have well-developed molariform teeth - it might, like Chimaerasuchus, have included plants in its diet.

facts.statement: Due to insufficient preservation of key jaw bones, it is debated whether Adamantinasuchus could chew plants; however, the lack of wear on its teeth suggests it was likely only capable of dorsoventral biting motions and ate softer food than plants.
facts.quote: There is insufficient preservation of the quadrate or the articular bones to tell whether its jaw was capable of back-and-forth movements necessary for chewing plants, but the relative lack of wear on its molariform teeth suggest that it was probably only capable of dorsoventral biting motions, not chewing, and that it mainly ate softer food than plants.

facts.statement: Adamantinasuchus belongs to the suborder Notosuchia.
facts.quote: subordo: Notosuchia

facts.statement: Adamantinasuchus is classified within the unranked family Ziphosuchia.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Ziphosuchia

facts.statement: Adamantinasuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in Brazil.
facts.quote: Adamantinasuchus is an extinct genus of notosuchian crocodylomorph from and named after the Late Cretaceous Adamantina Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus name combines the geological formation Adamantina with the Greek word for crocodile, while the species name honors the paleontologist William Roberto Nava who discovered the fossils.
facts.quote: El nombre del género deriva de Adamantina, en referencia a la formación geológica en la cual se encontró al holotipo, y el término griego souchos, "cocodrilo"; y el nombre de la especie, navae, es un homenaje a William Roberto Nava, el paleontólogo que realizó el descubrimiento de los fósiles.

facts.statement: Remains were discovered in the Adamantina Formation near Marília, São Paulo, Brazil, during dam construction.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron descubiertos en la Formación Adamantina en la región de Marília en el estado de São Paulo en Brasil durante la construcción de una represa

facts.statement: Excavations yielded approximately 7 specimens, mostly cranial material, some postcranial parts, and dozens of isolated bone elements.
facts.quote: Se hallaron en las excavaciones cerca de 7 especímenes, principalmente de materiales craneanos y algunos pocos postcraneanos, además de varias decenas de elementos óseos aislados.

facts.statement: The small size of the bones suggests the animal was about 0.50 centimeters long when alive.
facts.quote: El tamaño reducido de los huesos indica que en vida el animal podría medir en torno a los 0,50 centímetros de longitud.

facts.statement: The skull was relatively small with large eye sockets measuring approximately 60 millimeters in length and 30 in height.
facts.quote: Adamantinasuchus tiene un cráneo relativamente pequeño con cuencas oculares grandes, las cuales miden aproximadamente 60 milímetros de largo y 30 de alto.

facts.statement: It was likely a carnivore or omnivore that fed on small vertebrates or animal carcasses.
facts.quote: Adamantinasuchus fue probablemente carnívoro u omnívoro y se alimentaría de pequeños vertebrados, o de cadáveres de animales.

facts.statement: Sharp front teeth were presumably used for cutting, while posterior molar-like teeth served for crushing.
facts.quote: Los dientes afilados en la parte delantera de los incisivos y caninos de la mandíbula como se utilizaron presumiblemente para cortar, mientras que los dientes posteriores, similares a molares, servirían para aplastar.

facts.statement: While occasionally classified in the family Sphagesauridae, some phylogenetic analyses suggest it is closely related to the genera Yacarerani or Pakasuchus rather than Sphagesaurus.
facts.quote: Ha sido clasificado ocasionalmente en la familia Sphagesauridae, aunque algunos análisis filogenéticos sugieren que puede estar estrechamente relacionado con los géneros Yacarerani o Pakasuchus y no con Sphagesaurus.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Turonian or Santonian ages.
facts.quote: y datan de las épocas del Turoniense o Santoniense.

facts.statement: The time range is recorded as Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
